goals.item: A trainer can see their training sessions in one place.
A trainer can narrow the list by session status.
A trainer can add a new session with a title and a future start date/time, and see it in the list.
Scope stays small. Nothing outside view, filter and create is added.

group.name: Viewing sessions
group.item: Sessions load automatically when the trainer opens the workspace.
Each session shows its title, status and start date/time.
A loading indication is shown while sessions are loading.
If loading fails, one understandable error state is shown.
The trainer can retry from that error state.
If there are no sessions to show, a short "no sessions" message is displayed.

group.name: Filtering sessions
group.item: The trainer can choose `All` or exactly one status.
A chosen status shows only sessions with that status.

group.name: Creating a session
group.item: The trainer can open a create form with a title and a start date/time.
The title is trimmed and must be 3 to 80 characters long.
The date/time must be in the future.
Invalid input produces a useful message that explains what to fix.
While a create request is pending, repeated submission is prevented.
A successfully created session gets a default initial status.
A successfully created session is added to the visible list. If a status filter is active, it appears only when it matches that filter.
After success, the form closes and resets.
If creation fails, a message is shown, the entered values are kept, and the trainer can resubmit.

acceptance-criteria.item: Opening the workspace shows loaded sessions with title, status and start date/time.
A loading indication is visible while the request is pending.
A failed load shows an error state that the trainer can recover from.
An empty result shows a "no sessions" message.
Picking a status shows only matching sessions, and picking `All` shows every session again.
A title that is empty, whitespace-only, shorter than 3 characters or longer than 80 characters is rejected with a message.
A title of exactly 3 or exactly 80 characters is accepted, regardless of surrounding spaces.
A missing or non-future date/time is rejected with a message.
Submitting a valid form creates exactly one session, even with repeated submit attempts while pending.
After a successful create, the session is visible under `All`, and the form is closed and reset.
After a failed create, the trainer sees a message and the entered values are preserved.
The trainer can complete the whole flow: open, filter, create, then see the new session.
At least one automated test covers the main flow, for example filtering or successful creation, by checking what the trainer sees.
The flow has been tried once in a real browser, and what was actually seen is recorded.
Anything not done or not checked is reported as such.

out-of-scope.item: Session details, drawers or deep links
A complete API contract or scenario matrix
CI, deployment or a public URL
Strict TypeScript migration or unrelated refactoring
Production-grade concerns beyond the above. This is a training exercise, so session ordering and additional session fields are not required.

assumptions.item: The status values in the filter are not specified. Any reasonable choice is acceptable.
The default status for a new session is not specified. Any reasonable choice from those status values is acceptable.
The date format and timezone for "future date/time" are not specified. Any reasonable choice is acceptable.
The wording of error and validation messages is not specified. Any reasonable choice is acceptable.
Session order in the list is not specified. Any order is acceptable.
A session consists of title, status and start date/time only.
Only the trainer's flow is covered, with no other users, sign-in or permissions.
Data comes from a mock API, and no real backend is built.
The mock approach, existing stack and unrelated-code constraints in TASK.md are delivery conditions for later roles, not business requirements.
